title: TC-EXP-301-05 asserts on measured wall-clock backoff deltas, which are not stable under parallel test load
symptom: TC-EXP-301-05 fails at tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig:693 on `try testing.expect(observed_delta_ms >= lower_bound)`. It reads EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM next_attempt_at) before and after Queue.markRetry and asserts the difference is within +/-500ms of the expected backoff delay.
root_cause_analysis: The assertion measures a wall-clock delta between two database reads. Roughly 20 test binaries contend for the same PostgreSQL instance under `zig build test-integration-svc`, and the +/-500ms tolerance is smaller than the scheduling jitter that contention produces. The property under test (backoff grows on the expected schedule) is real; the way it is measured is not deterministic.
impact: 1 of the 3 remaining effects_subsystem_test failures. Flaky rather than permanently red, which is worse for signal: it makes the suite's pass/fail non-reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: TC-EXP-301-05 asserts on a deterministic property (e.g. the ordering and relative spacing of the recorded next_attempt_at values, or the value Queue.markRetry computes) rather than on a measured elapsed wall-clock delta
The assertion still fails if the backoff schedule regresses — it must not be weakened into a tautology
The block passes repeatedly under a loaded parallel run
related: ISS-0158 / GH #479 - the run that isolated this as a distinct cause
ISS-0182 / GH #515 - this is the surviving half of that issue; its leak half was fixed under ISS-0158
notes: Filed per CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only' and the 'filed and forwarded, not fixed here' scope boundary. ISS-0158 fixed 5 root causes (11 blocks, 0 regressions); this cluster has a distinct root cause and belongs in its own run.
